dialogue_text: Thirty days, Conrad. That's what I said. Every penny. Move your junk off the sidewalk. Yes, sir.
...Luke? Hi, Hannah.
...Luke? Hi, Hannah. Hannah. Oh my God. It's really you.
Hannah. Don't touch him. Spencer, it's Luke. Luke Bennett. From Northbrook.
Spencer Hale. So he's the one you married. Sorry. Have we met?
Sorry. Have we met? We have. You're the reason Northbrook threw me out. Spencer, what is he talking about?
He stole my watch sophomore year. The whole campus knew.
Funny thing. You're still wearing it. Hannah. Car. Now.
Luke, where are you staying? I'm fine. Go on. Watch yourself, Spencer. The last thing you slipped into
The last thing you slipped into my bag cost me sixteen years.
Hannah. You dropped this.
My mother's. I just picked it up from the jeweler. They fixed the clasp. Thirty-six stones. I counted every one on the walk over,
I counted every one on the walk over, so nobody could ever say one went missing. Count them again when we get home.
That clasp's gonna open on you. They put the safety catch in backwards.
You still have those pliers. The ones with the chipped jaw. Never lost them. Let me help you. Please.
You already did. You said my name like I was still somebody. Drive.
“Have we met?” You knew exactly who he was.
“Have we met?” You knew exactly who he was. Of course I knew him. He was a thief, Hannah. The school kicked him out. He fixed my bike for a whole year and never took a cent.
He fixed my bike for a whole year and never took a cent. That's not a thief. And then he disappeared. No call. No note. Nothing. I'm
the one who stuck around. Who's Conrad? Business.
The Luke I knew was gonna build bridges. Plans changed. What happened to you?
What happened to you? Nobody hires a guy who got expelled for theft. Every application asks why you left Northbrook. My mom got worse.
My mom got worse. Then she was gone, and so was the house. I worked under the table at a garage for twelve years. The owner died, they shut it down.
This is my second winter out here. My dad's place needs a groundskeeper. Nothing there works anymore. Your husband won't let me past the front gate.
Your husband won't let me past the front gate. It's my father's land. It's my gate. I don't take what I didn't earn. Then earn it.
Why are you doing this? Because you walked out of my life without a single word. I want to know why.
I didn't walk out without a word, Hannah. Kid! Mugs! Coming.
Chain's snapped. Want me to fix it?
Want me to fix it? You can do that? If it's got a chain, wheels, or a motor, I can fix it. People are harder.
He's cute. Ask his name. What do I owe you? Your name. Hannah Caldwell.
Hannah Caldwell. Luke Bennett. Engineering. Scholarship kid. Hannah. Don't waste your time on the bike guy.
Hannah. Don't waste your time on the bike guy. Party at my place tonight. Can't, Spencer. I'm busy.
Next Friday, same time?
Next Friday, same time? It'll break again.
You pay me back out of your first paycheck. Gus— Go. And toss this thing.
And toss this thing. I'll find you a new one. This bag's been with me since college.
You must be the one Mrs. Hale picked up off the sidewalk.
You must be the one Mrs. Hale picked up off the sidewalk. Luke Bennett, ma'am. The new groundskeeper. Edna Mayhew. I've run this house for thirty years. That hasn't run since Mr.
That hasn't run since Mr. Caldwell passed. Cracked pump. Clogged line. Two days. We'll see.
Clogged line. Two days. We'll see. Luke. You shaved. You look nineteen. This place is beautiful. His?
This place is beautiful. His? Mine. Dad left it to me. Spencer just likes to say “my house.”
What is he doing at my house? Working. Luke's our new groundskeeper. Have you lost your mind?
He's a thief. Then keep an eye on him. I'm sure you will. Edna, lock up the silver.
It's been locked up for thirty years, Mr. Hale. One slip, Bennett. One. And you're back on your sidewalk.
One. And you're back on your sidewalk. Relax. I go through my own bag every morning now. Staff phone. My number's in it.
Staff phone. My number's in it. And one more thing. Every night the deer come up and eat Mr. Caldwell's roses.
He put that up himself. Deer camera. Anything moves, it records. Sound too. He never did figure out how it worked.
There's a little bill I still pay every month. He made me promise.
Mr. Caldwell never trusted that man. He used to say, a man who's only sweet while
He used to say, a man who's only sweet while his wife is watching is putting on a show.
Two days. Two days.
Conrad, listen to me. The land sells right after the party. Thirty-six million. You get your two and a half...
You get your two and a half... Collateral? Fine. Next Thursday. Something worth a lot more than your patience. Thirty days. You have my word.
Was that him again? Threatening you? It's handled. Next Saturday,
Next Saturday, the twenty-fourth. She signs. And she really thinks it's a villa on Lake Como? Anniversary present. It's Larkspur Hill.
It's Larkspur Hill. Every last vine. And then? Then you and I go see the real Lake Como.
Someone's out there.
It's the gardener's ladder. He fixes things. He was always fixing something back in school. Remember?
I remember everything about Northbrook. Paige Lennox.
Paige Lennox. Hannah's college roommate. She swore to the dean she watched me take Spencer's watch. And tonight she's in his arms.
And tonight she's in his arms. Paige Lennox? Her maid of honor? Good Lord. A week from Saturday, Hannah signs this place away.
A week from Saturday, Hannah signs this place away. She thinks she's getting a villa in Italy. Your word against her husband and her best friend?
Your word against her husband and her best friend? You'd be back on the street before lunch. I can't just stand there and watch her sign.
Leave the papers to me. You look after Hannah. What does that mean? Good night, Luke.
First roses the deer didn't get in three years.
Hannah. I need to tell you something. About Spencer and Paige. Last night, in the study. I saw them together.
The day we buried my father, Paige held my hand through the whole thing. She also lied to the dean.
She also lied to the dean. Told him she saw me take that watch. Stop it! When you vanished, Paige was the one who stayed. You didn't even leave a note.
You didn't even leave a note. I left a letter. I gave it to Paige. There was no letter, Luke.
Is the help bothering you again, honey? Ten days on the job and he's already making up stories. I saw you, Spencer. You and Paige.
You and Paige. You saw me give my wife's best friend a hug. Prove it. The same way you proved you didn't take my watch.
Where's my letter, Spencer? What letter? There's no letter. Just a bitter drifter with a grudge. You should have stayed on your sidewalk, Bennett.
I did. Your wife pulled me off it. Then I'll put you back.
Mom, it took three summers at the garage. Is it too small? She'll say yes, sweetheart.
Last day of the semester. Noon. On the stone bridge. Where I fixed her bike.
Nice ring, Bennett. Where does a scholarship kid get money for that? I earned it. Scholarships are fragile things.
Scholarships are fragile things. One little scandal and... Mr. Hale's watch. It was found in your backpack. I never touched his watch.
I never touched his watch. Somebody put it there. Miss Lennox. Tell me what you saw. I saw Luke take it, sir.
I saw Luke take it, sir. Right out of Spencer's locker. Paige... why would you say that?
I don't want to press charges, sir. I just want my watch back. Your scholarship is revoked.
Your scholarship is revoked. You're expelled. Sir, my mother's sick. That scholarship is all we have.
Clear out your room tonight, Mr. Bennett. I have to see Hannah.
She went home to her dad's for the weekend. And she doesn't want to see you. She won't believe them. Give her this.
Give her this. Please. Everything's in here. Promise me. I promise. Burn it.
I promise. Burn it. No. I hang on to anything useful.
Bottom drawer's been stuck for a month. It's Thursday. He's out golfing till six. Get it fixed before he notices. If that “villa” contract is anywhere in this house,
If that “villa” contract is anywhere in this house, it's in that desk. Mr. Caldwell had this put in. It keeps a record every time it opens.
It keeps a record every time it opens. He loved that sort of thing.
That's my handwriting. What is it? The letter. The one I gave Paige sixteen years ago.
The letter. The one I gave Paige sixteen years ago. He kept it. It's still sealed. Then Hannah never got it. Take it. It's yours. It always was.
He's early. What are you doing at my desk?
Fixing the drawer. Edna asked me to.
Dad's fountain.
Dad's fountain. You actually fixed it. Two days. Like I told Edna. Why did you really leave? I called for months. Your number was disconnected.
Your number was disconnected. I sold my phone to pay for Mom's medicine. After she died, all I had left was that bag. You could have come back.
You could have come back. I did come back. I waited for you once. You never showed.
You never showed. Waited? Where? Luke, what are you talking about? Hannah, there's something you need to—
Whatever it is, it waits till after Saturday. I have to get through this party. Please don't make me fall apart right now.
Okay. Saturday, after the party. When you're alone. Mrs. Hale, the caterers are asking for you.
The letter's gone? You kept it for sixteen years? Are you out of your mind? I told you. I hang on to anything useful.
I told you. I hang on to anything useful. You're sure it was him? He was at my desk this afternoon. If she reads it, she starts asking about that watch. And then about me.
Then we give her something else to look at. We turn him back into a thief. Saturday night, with the whole party watching.
with the whole party watching. How? Her mother's necklace. He held that box on the sidewalk. His prints are all over it. Just like Northbrook.
Just like Northbrook. The necklace is in the safe. Leave the safe to me. You just make sure it turns up in his bag.
You just make sure it turns up in his bag. And if my letter's in there, bring it to me.
Conrad? Tonight. Ten-thirty, your office. That collateral you wanted, I'll bring it myself. Don't call me again before Monday.
This one's clean. But I've been Henry's lawyer for forty years, Spencer. Anything that touches this estate comes through me first.
Anything that touches this estate comes through me first. Those were his orders. It's just a villa, Arthur. An anniversary present. I'll have to slip out at nine tomorrow night.
I'll have to slip out at nine tomorrow night. My wife's birthday. Tomorrow night you're pouring drinks. The vest's in the kitchen. I'm the groundskeeper.
Tomorrow night you're whatever I say you are. Smile. It's a party. Gone by nine. Of course he is.
Gone by nine. Of course he is. Everyone! This is Luke. Hannah's little charity project.
Hannah's little charity project. She found him on a sidewalk. Does he do tricks? Only with other people's watches.
Spencer. That's enough. He's working. Leave him alone. It's fine, Hannah. Champagne, ma'am?
It's fine, Hannah. Champagne, ma'am? Where's Mom's necklace? I want to wear it tonight. In the safe, honey. Edna's bringing it out for the toast.
Happy anniversary, you two. Spencer, signed copy on my desk Monday. I'm just going to call my mom.
Mr. Hale... the box in the safe. It's empty. Empty? My mother's diamonds?
Empty? My mother's diamonds? Everyone stay right where you are. The police are already on their way.
Detective Alvarez, county police. Who called this in? I did. Detective,
I did. Detective, there's one person here tonight who held that necklace on a sidewalk. One person here who got thrown out of college for stealing. Spencer, don't.
Where's your bag, Bennett? In the tool shed. Go look. Oh, I will.
Look what our groundskeeper takes home at night.
Look what our groundskeeper takes home at night. Her mother's diamonds, in a homeless man's bag.
Luke. Tell me it wasn't you. Hannah, look at me. He pulled this exact thing sixteen years ago.
He pulled this exact thing sixteen years ago. Same bag. Same trick. Give it up. A thief's a thief. Ask Paige where she went after nine.
Out front, on the phone with my mother. Ask anyone. Mrs. Hale. Do you want to press charges? Of course she does.
No. No charges. ...I just want him gone.
There was a letter in that bag, Hannah. Now it's gone. Ask those two where it went.
Ask those two where it went. He's lost it, Detective. It's a long walk back to the sidewalk.
It's a long walk back to the sidewalk. Don't come back. The necklace goes in, the letter comes out. This time you wanted the letter back too.
This time you wanted the letter back too. I'm so sorry, sweetie.
I wanted to warn you. I'm such an idiot. I wanted him to still be the boy I remembered.
Soft heart. That's why you've got me. Sign your anniversary present, and next week we fly out to see it.
Shouldn't Arthur look at it first? He went through every page yesterday. I was right there on the porch. I watched Arthur read the whole thing.
I watched Arthur read the whole thing. I just chose you over him in front of everyone.
I just chose you over him in front of everyone. I'm not going to start doubting you now. You deserve something beautiful tonight.
I'm sleeping in the guest room tonight. I need to be alone.
Thought you'd made it, kid. I did. For seventeen days.
What happened? Somebody put a necklace in my bag. Just like college. Where's that bag been hanging all week?
Where's that bag been hanging all week? On a hook in the tool shed. Right under the... Right under that deer camera. Anything moves, it records. Sound too.
Anything moves, it records. Sound too. Who you calling at this hour? The one person in that house who's never lied to me.
Edna. The camera over the tool shed. Leave the back gate open for me.
It's in, Spencer. ...The letter? Hang on.
It's in, Spencer. ...The letter? Hang on. Got it. I'll bring it up. In Mr. Caldwell's shed.
In Mr. Caldwell's shed. He didn't even have to look.
Monday, nine a.m., Kessler comes to sign. Then the land's ours. She won't know a thing till the bulldozers roll in.
She won't know a thing till the bulldozers roll in. She signed tonight, Luke. I saw the papers on his desk when I locked up. Then we've got till Monday morning.
Then we've got till Monday morning. You've got me.
You shouldn't be here. If Spencer sees you and— Five minutes. Then I go back to my sidewalk, and you never have to see me again. How did you know I'd be out here?
How did you know I'd be out here? Edna told me you walk out here every morning.
That's Paige... She said she was calling her mom. She was calling your husband. ...Show me the rest.
Yeah, I... Ten years. Ten anniversaries.
Ten years. Ten anniversaries. And my best friend. I'm sorry, Hannah. You said there was a letter.
He kept it locked in his desk for sixteen years. Last night, when Paige planted the necklace, she took it out of my bag. The camera caught that too.
Then what I signed last night... Wasn't a villa. It was Larkspur Hill. Every last vine.
A developer named Kessler comes to sign Monday at nine. Then Monday, we're in that room too.
Last night I asked you to tell me it wasn't you. I should have known. You couldn't have. That's exactly what they were counting on.
I've seen the video. I also pulled the 911 records. Look at the time on your husband's call.
That's before I ever opened the safe. So either he guessed,
or he knew it was gone before anybody did. That's not enough yet. If he lies about it to my face, it is.
If he lies about it to my face, it is. Throw in what you signed last night, and I'm looking at fraud. Can you stop the sale?
Monday at nine, I'll be in that room. Until then, don't let them see it coming. Mr. Bennett.
Mr. Bennett. I owe you an apology. Just be on time, Detective. That safe of yours really keeps a log?
Every time it opens. Bring it Monday.
I couldn't sleep either. Your favorite. You always know what I need. That's what best friends are for.
Can I ask you something? Did you really see Luke take Spencer's watch? With my own eyes. I told the dean everything.
And he really never left me a letter? Nothing, Hannah. He just ran. Guys like him always do. You've always been so brave, Paige. So honest.
You've always been so brave, Paige. So honest. For you? Always.
Three hundred luxury homes. Larkspur Hill won't recognize itself. That's the idea. Let's get it signed.
Let's get it signed. Your wife's not joining us? She's resting. Saturday wore her out. She's already signed everything she needs to.
I'm not resting, Spencer. Honey. You should be in bed.
Good morning. I'm exactly where I should be. Good morning, Mr. Kessler. I hear you're buying my father's land. Your land. That's what you told me.
Your land. That's what you told me. Before anyone signs, Mr. Kessler, you should know this. The week Hannah got married, Henry put this estate in a trust.
Henry put this estate in a trust. Selling a single vine takes two trustees. Hannah is one. The other, Henry picked himself, and told me to keep
The other, Henry picked himself, and told me to keep the name quiet until somebody tried to sell. That would be me, Mr. Hale.
That would be me, Mr. Hale. I don't sign for liars.
And one more thing. On Friday, Spencer showed me a contract for a villa. These signature pages were not in it when I reviewed it.
You told me this deal was clean. We're done here. You're letting the gardener turn you against me?
You're letting the gardener turn you against me? He didn't have to, Spencer. You did that all by yourself. And this is my house. It always was.
It always was. Mr. Hale. Saturday night, you called 911 at 9:05. Because the necklace had been stolen.
Mrs. Mayhew didn't find the box empty until 9:22. I checked the safe myself at eight. It was there. The safe keeps a log.
The safe keeps a log. On Saturday, nobody opened it before 9:22. The last time before that was Thursday morning, 7:50. Your code.
And at 9:05 you told dispatch, “Our groundskeeper stole my wife's necklace.” Seven minutes later, here's where that necklace was.
here's where that necklace was. Hannah, I can explain—
The way you explained it to the dean sixteen years ago? Paige? What were you doing in the tool shed? I had no idea about any of this.
I had no idea about any of this. I want a lawyer.
Spencer Hale, you're under arrest for filing a false report, fraud, and conspiracy.
Ten years, Hannah. You'd throw it all away for a bum off the street? No. For the truth.
No. For the truth. Mrs. Hale, we'll need the necklace as evidence.
Hannah... this isn't the clasp I bent. What? The catch I fixed on the sidewalk.
The catch I fixed on the sidewalk. My pliers leave a little notch. There's no notch on this one.
And real diamonds don't hold a fog. Then where are my mother's diamonds?
Then where are my mother's diamonds? Ask him. Thursday morning I took the necklace out to get it cleaned. Left it in my desk drawer.
Left it in my desk drawer. Thursday afternoon, who was alone in my study with that drawer open? He walked out with the real one
He walked out with the real one and left a fake in its place. Then on Saturday, Paige, God knows why,
God knows why, grabbed whatever was in my drawer and stuck it in his bag. Ask her.
He wasn't alone. I was in that room the whole time. She's been covering for him since the day he showed up.
The only thing I took out of that drawer was my letter. So you did take something out of that drawer. A college thief,
a fake in his bag, and the real diamonds gone. Do your job, Detective. Two minutes ago you said you checked the safe at eight.
I got the day wrong. Not the necklace. Whether I believe him doesn't matter. The real diamonds are gone,
The real diamonds are gone, you admit you were in that drawer, and the only witness is the woman who let you in.
Mr. Bennett, you're coming down to the station with me. No— You say your pliers leave a notch.
You say your pliers leave a notch. What I've got is your word, a pair of chipped pliers, and a college expulsion for theft.
And a man who called 911 seventeen minutes before anyone knew. You said it yourself this morning.
Saturday night, in front of everyone, I asked him to tell me it wasn't him. This time I'm not asking.
I don't have enough to hold you tonight, Mr. Bennett. You're free to go. You don't leave the county. The district attorney decides
The district attorney decides on Friday whether to charge you. Felony theft. Every time somebody doesn't believe me,
Every time somebody doesn't believe me, I have to live those sixteen years all over again. And every time you stand next to me, they take something from you. Your husband. Your best friend. Your
mother's diamonds. Go home, Hannah. That is my home. And you're still my groundskeeper. Seven a.m. tomorrow.
And you're still my groundskeeper. Seven a.m. tomorrow. I'll be there. Not for us. To finish what started sixteen years ago.
The judge let you walk out on your own signature, Spencer.
The judge let you walk out on your own signature, Spencer. Two and a half million, and now the land's gone too. What exactly does that leave you? My wife. She'll pay anything
My wife. She'll pay anything for her mother's diamonds, Conrad. And while she's paying you, the police will be busy deciding the gardener stole them.
And if she won't pay? Then they go to Antwerp. Stone by stone. She'll never see them again. You can't set foot on that estate.
You can't set foot on that estate. Order of protection. I don't need to. You do.
The detective dropped this off this morning. Wanted an opinion from the shop that fixed the original.
Wanted an opinion from the shop that fixed the original. Cubic zirconia. Nice work, made from photographs. A piece like this takes six weeks at the very least.
A piece like this takes six weeks at the very least. Six weeks ago, Luke was still on the sidewalk.
Your mother's necklace. Thirty-six stones, each one on file. Look at the safety catch. Backwards. That same afternoon
Look at the safety catch. Backwards. That same afternoon I straightened it out on the sidewalk. My pliers leave a notch.
Backwards. That one's on us, I'm afraid. But son, without the real necklace, it's still your pliers against his drawer.
it's still your pliers against his drawer. Then we get the real one back.
Conrad Rourke, Mrs. Hale. Your husband pledged this against a loan of two and a half million.
The loan is past due. I'm a reasonable man. Pay his debt by Friday, and it comes home. If not, it leaves the country.
If not, it leaves the country. One stone at a time. He had no right to pledge it. It's mine.
He had no right to pledge it. It's mine. Then take that up with him. Friday.
Don't pay him. If you pay, Spencer wins. His debt's gone, and I'm still the guy who stole your diamonds. If I get it back,
If I get it back, your notch is on that clasp. That's the only thing that clears you. Not with your money. Not for me. It's my mother's necklace. It's my money.
And this time, I'm the one choosing.
If he hands it to you in person and tells you who pledged it, I can charge him. Receiving stolen property. Extortion. Then I'll pay him. You'll wear a wire.
You'll wear a wire. And the check has to be real. Men like him can smell a setup. If he smells it, he walks, and so does your necklace.
I'm going with her. He'll have to let somebody check it. You're one phone call away from a felony charge, Mr. Bennett. That's why I'm going.
That's why I'm going.
Heard Conrad stopped by. Just pay him, honey, and all of this goes away. Even your gardener. We'll see on Friday, Spencer.
Mind if I take a look?
That's the one. ...thirty-four, thirty-five, thirty-six.
A collateral receipt. Signed by your husband. Thursday, October twenty-second, ten-forty p.m.
ten-forty p.m. Right here at this desk. All perfectly legal. Thursday night, ten-forty, the necklace was in his hand.
He told the police I walked off with it that afternoon. Conrad Rourke, you're under arrest for receiving
Conrad Rourke, you're under arrest for receiving stolen property and extortion. Stolen? Her husband pledged it— Pledging something that isn't yours has another name. Stealing.
This puts the real necklace in Spencer Hale's hands Thursday night. I'm telling the DA today. No theft

Thursday night. I'm telling the DA today. No theft charge, Mr. Bennett. Every stone has a certificate number, and the jeweler's photos are on file. We'll photograph it and log it. It's yours. Sign the release.
it and log it. It's yours. Sign the release.
That was the DA. An arrest warrant got signed an hour ago. Paige Lennox filed a sworn statement.
Paige Lennox filed a sworn statement. She says she was never in that shed. She says the memory card spent a whole night with you and Mrs. Mayhew, and that you two came to her door and threatened her.
and that you two came to her door and threatened her. Spencer's lawyer attached a private report. Two gaps in the timestamps, right before 9:12. “Signs of editing.”
A warrant for who? Two names. Yours and Mrs. Mayhew's. Fabricating evidence, and tampering with a witness. On that second one, a judge can set bail.
a judge can set bail. Edna's seventy-two. If that footage gets thrown out, Spencer's 911 call is just a man who panicked at a party.
Spencer's 911 call is just a man who panicked at a party. And the papers I signed are still out there. Arthur says Spencer's lawyer is asking a judge to suspend Edna as trustee while she's charged.
to suspend Edna as trustee while she's charged. Kessler's people are still calling. If somebody else takes her place, the land's back on the table.
I'm supposed to take you in right now. I'll drive you home first.
You and Mrs. Mayhew walk out of that house together. That's the most I can do.
Thirty years, I have never been late for anything. I won't start today.
Hannah, don't—
Night court set it at a hundred thousand apiece. I need collateral for both.
My mother's diamonds. For both of them.
Thirty-six. That covers both. Sign here.
You put up your mother's necklace. Saturday night it got you thrown out. Tonight it gets you out. That necklace already cost you once.
That necklace already cost you once. You didn't have to do that. Sixteen years ago, nobody paid a thing to get you out. Somebody should have.
The card has its own timestamps. They'll just say I faked those too. We need something I never could've touched.
...Mr. Caldwell's camera. That little bill. Nine ninety-nine a month, three years now.
He made me promise to keep paying it. I never knew what it actually did. It uploads. Every clip goes up to the camera
It uploads. Every clip goes up to the camera company the second it's recorded. Do you know the password? He never trusted anything he couldn't write down.
He never trusted anything he couldn't write down. All of it. The same second.
All of it. The same second. On their server. Nobody in this house could touch it. Thursday's hearing. This keeps the footage in.
Keeping the footage in won't make him confess. He's got a backup plan. He always has a backup plan.
You said he always has a backup. On Monday I only printed up to 9:22. Look at the next line. Saturday night, eleven forty-seven.
eleven forty-seven. He opened it one more time. After the party. What would he put in there after the party?
He didn't keep this letter for me. He kept it to hold over her. Six weeks ago.
Six weeks ago. The fake was picked up under her name. If anything went wrong, it would all land on her. Not one word in his handwriting.
Not one word in his handwriting. Not yet. I want to read it at the right time.
The originals go to Detective Alvarez first thing Monday. You keep the copies. And Hannah, his lawyer gets copies too.
And Hannah, his lawyer gets copies too. That's how it works. Whatever's in this folder, Spencer will try to use it.
Here to see me fall apart? He kept this for sixteen years.
He kept this for sixteen years. Not for me. For you. The day you ever told the truth about that watch,
The day you ever told the truth about that watch, he'd give it to me and say you were the one who hid it. In September, he sent you into the city to pick up a box.
In September, he sent you into the city to pick up a box. Give your name, don't open it. Right? What was in that box ended up in Luke's bag on Saturday.
The originals go to the police tomorrow. And on this slip, there's only one name. He said it was your anniversary present.
He said it was your anniversary present. He told me not to open it. ...On Monday, in that study, he threw me to the wolves. Twice.
...He kept saying Lake Como. He said a lot of things. To both of us.
...He was mine first, back in college. He picked you because of your father's land. He kept me because I'd do anything he asked.
He kept me because I'd do anything he asked. Why are you telling me any of this?
Sixteen years ago, you had one chance to tell the truth, and you didn't. On Thursday, you get another one. That's more than he ever gave Luke.
Sixteen years ago, you walked out of that dean's office with nothing. Today you get to stand here and watch her end up with nothing too. Then you'd better watch closely.
Then you'd better watch closely. People versus Spencer Hale. The defense moves to throw out the camera footage.
Ms. Lennox is here as a witness. Your Honor, according to Ms. Lennox's sworn statement and an independent analysis,
statement and an independent analysis, this memory card spent a night in the hands of a man expelled from college for theft and a housekeeper with a stake in this estate.
and a housekeeper with a stake in this estate. The timestamps have gaps. We move to exclude the footage entirely. The camera only records when something moves.
The camera only records when something moves. The company's motion log shows nothing moved during those gaps. And every clip went up to their server the second it was recorded.
to their server the second it was recorded. Until last weekend, nobody had logged into that account in three years. Their engineer certified it. The server copy matches the card frame for frame.
The server copy matches the card frame for frame. The footage comes in. Motion denied.
Your Honor, in light of that ruling, the People move to dismiss the related case against Mr. Bennett and Mrs. Mayhew. So ordered. The charges are dismissed,
